options.C: To list the medications paramedics must carry in an ambulance
options.D: To show hospital doctors how to perform surgery on heart patients

explanation: Think of the Chain of Survival as a team effort! It links early actions from bystanders and first responders to give the patient the best fighting chance.

question: Which of the following is NOT considered a harmful traditional practice?

options.A: Female genital mutilation performed without anesthesia
options.B: Forced physical practices during early puberty rites
options.C: Routine childhood immunizations against measles
options.D: Child marriage involving underage adolescents

explanation: Immunizations save children's lives from deadly diseases! They are a standard, safe medical intervention, unlike harmful cultural practices.

question: Which healthcare professional often acts as the central coordinator in palliative care teams?

options.A: The nurse
options.B: The pharmacist
options.C: The hospital administrator
options.D: The laboratory scientist

explanation: That's you! Because nurses spend the most time right at the bedside, we are the glue holding the care team and the family's communication together.

question: What is the main goal of community mobilisation in Primary Health Care?

options.A: Making people active partners in their own health
options.B: Allowing foreign donors to control local clinics
options.C: Reducing the cost of building government hospitals
options.D: Punishing communities that ignore public health advice

explanation: Community mobilisation shifts people from being passive receivers of care to active participants who help shape health programs. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which part of Nigeria generally records lower modern contraceptive prevalence rates?

options.A: Major coastal ports
options.B: Capital city districts
options.C: The Southern zones
options.D: The Northern zones

explanation: National health surveys consistently show differences in mCPR across regions, with the northern zones generally recording lower rates than the southern zones.

question: Which of these is NOT a form of social stigma for persons with physical disabilities?

options.A: Receiving appropriate medical rehabilitation therapies
options.B: Encountering buildings with no wheelchair ramps
options.C: Being excluded from community social gatherings
options.D: Facing derogatory language and public staring

explanation: Spot on! Rehab therapy is supportive healthcare. Staring, lack of ramps, and exclusion are unfair barriers and forms of stigma.

question: How do nurses use triage during a mass casualty incident?

options.A: By treating patients strictly on a first-come, first-served basis
options.B: By waiting for international doctors to arrive before touching any patient
options.C: By focusing only on patients who show no signs of physical injury
options.D: By sorting patients based on the urgency of their medical needs and survival chance

explanation: Exactly! Triage helps nurses quickly prioritize care so that the most critical patients get help first.

question: A nurse needs to assess circulation in a patient's foot after orthopedic surgery. Which pulse site should the nurse check?

options.A: Apical site
options.B: Brachial artery
options.C: Temporal artery
options.D: Dorsalis pedis

explanation: The dorsalis pedis pulse is located on the top of the foot and is used specifically to check blood flow to the lower extremities. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is a great community nursing strategy to help stop FGM?

options.A: Arresting family members immediately upon hearing rumors
options.B: Ignoring cultural beliefs and focusing strictly on hospital rules
options.C: Promoting alternative rites of passage that do not involve cutting
options.D: Training traditional practitioners to use sterile razor blades

explanation: Communities love celebrating their youth growing up! By supporting non-cutting ceremonies, we respect the culture while keeping our girls safe.

question: Why do nurses also view groups living far apart as a 'community' if they share a common bond?

options.A: Because government funding requires international grouping
options.B: Because modern hospitals treat all patients as a single population
options.C: Because physical geography has no impact on human health outcomes
options.D: Because they experience similar health challenges and support needs

explanation: Spot on! Even if people live in different towns, groups like nursing mothers or people with sickle cell share similar health needs that nurses can help support together.

question: Which group of patients is most at risk from drug-resistant infections?

options.A: Individuals living in high-altitude mountain regions
options.B: Young adult athletes with minor sports injuries
options.C: Healthy adults with strong nutritional status
options.D: Immunocompromised patients and neonates

explanation: Exactly right. Newborns and patients with weak immune systems don't have enough backup to fight off tough, resistant bugs when standard medicines fail. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h5)

question: What does 'replacement cost pricing' mean in a changing economy?

options.A: Waiting for the government to fix market prices before selling any drugs
options.B: Selling all medicines at half price when they are close to their expiration date
options.C: Pricing drugs based on how much it will cost to buy new stock tomorrow
options.D: Charging patients the exact same price the manufacturer set ten years ago

explanation: Replacement pricing ensures that the money you collect today is enough to buy brand-new stock at current market prices.

question: What is normal regarding a woman's fertility after she stops taking DMPA injections?

options.A: Fertility returns instantly within twenty-four hours
options.B: There can be a delay of several months before ovulation resumes
options.C: Fertility is permanently destroyed after one year of use
options.D: Fertility only returns if surgical intervention is performed

explanation: Because the hormone lingers in the body tissues, it can take a few months for ovulation and regular cycles to bounce back after stopping.

question: What does sustainability mean for a community health program?

options.A: The community can maintain the program after external funding ends
options.B: The program receives unlimited money from the government forever
options.C: Foreign experts run the project without stopping
options.D: No evaluation is ever required after setup

explanation: A sustainable program is built to last using local capacity and resources so it does not collapse when outside donors depart. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h6)

question: What is a key question a nurse can ask to assess food security in a patient?

options.A: What is your exact family income down to the last dollar?
options.B: Do you prefer eating white bread or whole grain bread?
options.C: Do you worry about running out of food before getting more money?
options.D: How many hours of physical exercise do you do each week?

explanation: Screening for food security involves asking direct, simple questions about running out of food and lacking money to buy more. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h8)

question: A head nurse wants to know if a newly introduced fall-prevention bundle actually decreases patient falls over the next year on the surgical ward. Which action represents applying prospective thinking?

options.A: Implementing the bundle today and tracking fall rates prospectively over the coming year
options.B: Interviewing staff nurses about falls that occurred before they were born
options.C: Asking elderly patients to guess why they might fall in the future
options.D: Looking up incident reports from five years ago to see how many people slipped

explanation: Applying a measure today and observing future outcomes embodies the core methodology of prospective clinical research. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h7)

question: What is the main difference between an antiseptic and a disinfectant?

options.A: Antiseptics are heated before use, while disinfectants are kept at room temperature.
options.B: Antiseptics are used on living tissue, while disinfectants are used on inanimate surfaces.
options.C: Disinfectants are safe to drink, while antiseptics are strictly for external wounds.
options.D: Disinfectants kill viruses, while antiseptics only kill bacteria and fungi.

explanation: Antiseptics are formulated to be safe enough for human skin and wounds, whereas disinfectants are harsh chemicals meant only for objects and furniture. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h1)

question: Why do we call patient assessment in the intensive care unit a continuous loop?

options.A: Because vital signs never change in stable patients
options.B: Because doctors only visit patients once a day
options.C: Because hospital computers demand hourly data entry
options.D: Because interventions require constant re-evaluation

explanation: Think of it as a cycle: you assess, you act, and then you immediately check how the patient responded. It keeps repeating to keep them safe!

question: Why are newborn babies born with soft spots and flexible skull bones?

options.A: To allow the skull bones to overlap during birth and accommodate rapid brain growth
options.B: To let the cerebrospinal fluid drain easily through the scalp tissues
options.C: To prevent the brain from expanding too quickly before walking begins
options.D: To keep the infant's head cool during high fevers in the first year

explanation: Spot on! That flexibility helps the baby's head squeeze safely through the birth canal and gives the brain plenty of room to grow fast afterwards.

question: What is the main danger of waiting for lab test results before treating certain severe poisonings?

options.A: Immediate kidney failure from drawing too much blood
options.B: Severe allergic reactions to the laboratory reagents
options.C: Automatic rejection of insurance claims by the hospital
options.D: Dangerous delays in giving life-saving therapy

explanation: In toxicology emergencies, clinical signs matter more than paperwork. Waiting on lab results can waste precious time while the poison takes over.

question: If you are working right next to active X-ray or C-arm machines in the theatre, what protective wear must you wear?

options.A: Sterile waterproof surgical gowns
options.B: Thick rubber washing gloves
options.C: N95 nose masks
options.D: Lead aprons and thyroid shields

explanation: Radiation from imaging machines is powerful stuff! We use dense barriers like lead aprons and shields to keep our tissues safe from harm.

question: A flexible scope touches a patient's mucous membranes during a test. According to the Spaulding rule, how should this item be processed?

options.A: Standard low-level wiping
options.B: Terminal steam sterilization
options.C: Simple soap and water washing
options.D: High-level disinfection

explanation: Items touching mucous membranes are semi-critical! While they don't always need full autoclaving, they definitely need high-level disinfection to knock out stubborn germs and viruses.

question: What do we call a pregnancy where a mother is carrying two or more babies at the same time?

options.A: Singleton pregnancy
options.B: Ectopic pregnancy
options.C: Multiple pregnancy
options.D: Molar pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! A multiple pregnancy just means carrying more than one fetus—like twins, triplets, or more. You've got this!

question: A patient with terminal cancer feels too tired to finish three standard meals a day. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Stopping all oral intake immediately
options.B: Offering small, frequent, nutrient-dense portions
options.C: Switching entirely to thick liquid supplements
options.D: Forcing them to finish the plate before resting

explanation: Brilliant choice! Breaking food down into tiny, easy-to-manage snacks saves their energy and prevents them from feeling overwhelmed.

question: What is the primary benefit of establishing a coordinated referral pathway for GBV survivors?

options.A: It prevents the survivor from having to repeat their traumatic story to every new agency
options.B: It guarantees that the perpetrator will receive a life prison sentence
options.C: It eliminates the need for nurses to document physical injuries
options.D: It automatically lowers the hospital's electricity and water bills

explanation: Seamless coordination reduces secondary trauma by sparing survivors from retelling painful details at every step. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h7)

question: Why are pregnant women more prone to developing urinary tract infections?

options.A: White blood cells are absent from the body during gestation
options.B: High blood pressure forces bacteria directly into the bladder
options.C: The kidneys stop producing urine entirely for long stretches
options.D: Ureters and the renal pelvis dilate and urine flow slows down

explanation: Hormonal relaxation and physical compression cause urinary stasis in the dilated ureters, giving bacteria an easier environment to multiply. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h3)

question: Why does the surface of the brain have so many folds and grooves?

options.A: To improve the circulation of cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: To increase the surface area for more neurons
options.C: To separate the left and right sides of the body
options.D: To absorb physical shock from head injuries

explanation: Folding packs a massive amount of brain power into a small space, giving us room for lots of nerve cells!

question: What is a major drawback of using an autocratic leadership style on a general medical ward for too long?

options.A: It lowers staff morale and creativity
options.B: It makes doctors lose respect for nurses
options.C: It causes chaos during emergency resuscitations
options.D: It slows down emergency response times

explanation: When staff never get to share their ideas or feel heard, morale drops and creative problem-solving disappears. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h2)

question: A patient comes to your clinic with severe watery diarrhea and sudden, rapid dehydration after eating food from a roadside vendor. What condition should you suspect first?

options.A: Cholera
options.B: Asthma exacerbation
options.C: Chronic hypertension
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: You nailed it. Sudden, severe watery diarrhea and rapid dehydration after eating questionable food are classic red flags for cholera. Quick fluid replacement is key here!

question: What is the main difference between presumptive and probable signs of pregnancy?

options.A: Probable signs only show up right before birth
options.B: Presumptive signs are things the mother feels herself, while probable signs are things a nurse or doctor observes
options.C: Presumptive signs mean the baby is healthy, while probable signs mean trouble
options.D: Presumptive signs need lab tests, while probable signs need X-rays

explanation: Think of presumptive as what the client experiences (like nausea) and probable as what we find during our physical checks as clinicians!

question: What is the go-to emergency medication used to quickly reverse an opioid overdose?

options.A: Flumazenil
options.B: Naloxone
options.C: Atropine
options.D: Activated charcoal

explanation: Naloxone is a lifesaver! It quickly rushes in, kicks opioids off their brain receptors, and helps restore normal breathing almost instantly.

question: Why do patients often forget to mention herbs and local remedies during a drug history?

options.A: These substances dissolve completely in the body within minutes
options.B: Doctors automatically know every herb sold in local markets
options.C: They view them as food or lifestyle items, not real drugs
options.D: Federal law prohibits patients from discussing herbs in hospitals

explanation: Patients view everyday teas and herbal mixtures as harmless, so they don't think to mention them. Asking probing questions bridges this gap!

question: When should the nurse wash their hands during a home visit bag procedure?

options.A: Right after placing the bag on the floor
options.B: Only if the patient asks for hand sanitization
options.C: Only after finishing all tasks and leaving the house
options.D: Before opening the bag and handling clean equipment

explanation: Hand hygiene is performed before touching clean kit items to avoid transferring germs from the outside world onto sterile or clean supplies. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h4)

question: How do school health programs help students do better in their studies?

options.A: By guaranteeing admission to higher education
options.B: By replacing traditional classroom teaching hours
options.C: By eliminating the need for private tutoring
options.D: By reducing absences caused by preventable illnesses

explanation: Spot on! When kids are healthy and miss fewer classes due to preventable sicknesses, they stay on top of their lessons.

question: A patient requesting a medical abortion has an intrauterine device (IUD) in place. What needs to happen first?

options.A: The IUD must be removed before the medications are administered
options.B: The dose of misoprostol should be doubled to compensate for the IUD
options.C: The IUD should only be removed if heavy bleeding starts
options.D: The patient can take mifepristone while the IUD remains inside

explanation: Safety first! The IUD has to come out before starting to prevent heavy bleeding or nasty pelvic infections.

question: How can a severe lack of motivation among nursing staff endanger patient safety during a busy hospital shift?

options.A: Patients will refuse to take medications prescribed by unenthusiastic staff
options.B: Unmotivated nurses automatically lose their clinical license to administer drugs
options.C: Hospital administrators will immediately shut down the affected ward
options.D: Nurses may miss subtle signs of deterioration and rush through critical safety checks

explanation: When energy and motivation drop, it's easy to overlook small changes in a patient's condition or cut corners on vital safety checks. Stay sharp and stay safe!

question: A clinic nurse notices frequent shortages of basic drugs and sutures. What is a major reason for this in many African nations?

options.A: International agencies ban the importation of basic surgical items
options.B: Nurses generally mismanage the medical supplies in hospital warehouses
options.C: Patients refuse to accept free medications from the government
options.D: National health budgets frequently fall short of the Abuja Declaration target

explanation: When budgets fall short of targets like the Abuja 15%, clinics struggle to buy everyday essentials like gloves, drugs, and suture materials.
